messages:
Courtney M: Need a short, persuasive narrative for the launch webinar/announcement that ties performance to unit economics. Goal: 3 slides + 1 lead-capture CTA. Can we converge on the charts and the phrasing this afternoon?
Ravi S: +1. Audience = technical PMs/infra leads at PLG startups and platform teams. We should show both latency (user impact) and cost (ops impact).
Lina P: For charts: I suggest 1) 'Real request cost vs P95 latency' scatter with model variants as colors, 2) 'Throughput per GPU ($/1k tokens) by quantization/settings' bar chart, 3) a tiny flow showing routing options (hosted -> dedicated -> private) with approximate cost buckets.
Alex G: Love that. For slide copy, we should lead with a one-liner: "Ship predictable inference: faster responses, lower unit cost, simpler rollouts." Then 3 bullets tying each chart to a decision (choose variant, pick dedicated for scale, use routing to degrade gracefully).
Mike B: Can someone drop numbers we can plot? I can mock synthetic curves but prefer real profiled numbers (p95, p99, tokens/sec, $/1M tokens). Product or infra owners?
Ravi S: I have a perf dump for three representative workloads (chat, completion, embeddings). I'll share ranges: chat P95 120–220ms hosted, 35–70ms dedicated; cost per 1k tokens ~ $0.04 hosted baseline, $0.008 on dedicated w/quantization. Embeddings are cheaper per token but higher batch efficiency.
Lina P: Perfect — that gives us a good delta to show. For the scatter: x axis = P95 latency (ms), y axis = $/1k tokens, color = deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), marker size = throughput. Add a vertical line showing "interactive threshold" at 200ms.
Alex G: For visual treatment: keep colors friendly (blue = hosted, green = dedicated, purple = private). Use callouts: "2–5x lower per-token cost" and "p95 under interactive threshold" where applicable.
Courtney M: Copy tone: concise, product-forward, not too academic. Example line: "Reduce per-request cost up to 5x without sacrificing responsiveness — route automatically based on policy."
Mike B: I'll draft the slides and a small CSV for the charting library (vega). Quick example snippet I’ll use:
```
# sample rows
workload,deploy, p95_ms, cost_per_1k, throughput_tps
chat,hosted,180,0.04,12
chat,dedicated,55,0.008,45
embeddings,hosted,220,0.02,80
embeddings,dedicated,65,0.005,320
```
Ravi S: Nice. Also add an alternate trace showing cold-start slowpath for rare model variants — call it "fallback penalty" so we can justify routing rules.
Lina P: For the announcement copy/CTAs: 1) Short post announcing the benchmark findings with link to full report; 2) Webinar signup (title: "Serving LLMs at predictable latency and cost"); 3) Dedicated trial CTA for teams hitting >X qps. Keep forms minimal.
Alex G: Inbound routing: marketing needs the success condition — what is a qualified lead? UX + infra intent signals: created trial, API keys used >100k tokens within 30 days, or dedicated capacity request. Can ops send sample SLO questions for the form?
Mike B: I'll add a checkbox list in the webinar landing page for "we need SLA / private deployment / cost control" so sales can triage.
Courtney M: Next steps: Mike draft slides + CSV by EOD, Ravi export perf ranges into the shared sheet, Lina drafts 2 copy options (short post + webinar blurb). Alex to define inbound lead criteria. OpsBot: add a reminder?
OpsBot: Reminder set for 2024-11-05 15:00 UTC — follow-up sync to review slide draft. :bell:
Ravi S: I'll drop the perf sheet link in the channel once uploaded. If anyone wants different axes or a quick sim, ping me.
Lina P: I'll prep two headline variations for A/B: 1) "Predictable inference: slashed cost, kept latency" 2) "Keep users fast, cut your inference bill" — we'll test which performs better in early outreach.
Courtney M: Great. If we can get the mock visuals by EOD we'll run a quick design polish tomorrow. Thanks everyone :rocket:
